body:
I originally (incorrectly) interpreted browser behaviour as returning if the flag was set, basically: ```diff diff --git a/xhr.bs b/xhr.bs index e57f5f8..3b3c945 100644 --- a/xhr.bs +++ b/xhr.bs @@ -822,6 +822,8 @@

The send() method

Let processRequestBodyChunkLength, given a bytesLength, be these steps:

    +

  1. If this's upload complete is true, then return. +

  2. Increase requestBodyTransmitted by bytesLength.

  3. If not roughly 50ms have passed since these steps were last invoked, then return. @@ -829,7 +831,6 @@

    The send() method

  4. If this's upload listener is true, then fire a progress event named progress at this's upload object with requestBodyTransmitted and requestBodyLength. -

These steps are only invoked when new bytes are transmitted. @@ -838,6 +839,8 @@

The send() method

Let processRequestEndOfBody be these steps:

    +

  1. If this's upload complete is true, then return. +

  2. Set this's upload complete to true.

  3. If this's upload listener is false, then return. @@ -851,7 +854,6 @@

    The send() method

  4. Fire a progress event named loadend at this's upload object with requestBodyTransmitted and requestBodyLength.

-

  • Let processResponse, given a response, be these steps: ``` This matches the tests: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/xhr/send-redirect-post-upload.htm * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/xhr/send-entity-body-get-head-async.htm * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/xhr/open-during-abort-processing.htm But after thinking the implications of such a change through further, I don't think that's desirable, and XHR is missing some test coverage for _when_ the upload is considered complete. I think it should be when the final response arrives, but engines don't seem to have converged on that behaviour. From playing around with some tests locally, Firefox seems to have the behaviour I would expect (not the change I mention above), Chromium and Safari do not.
